features: Reel Import — Share an Instagram Reel to Echo Music: it identifies the song and asks you to confirm the match, then adds it to a playlist you choose — with an optional default playlist so future reels are added in one tap.
Reel Import suggestions: after adding a reel's song, songs from the same movie/album/artist are suggested so you can extend the vibe in one tap.
bug_fixes: Reel Import no longer prefills the manual search box with the uploader's Instagram handle: when identification fails, the search box now starts from the best song-name hint found (official audio attribution, then the caption's song marker/lyric fragment), and the same hint is kept when the app asks you to set up an Instagram session.

Reel Import gained one more identification stage: when official audio metadata and fingerprinting both come up empty, the creator's caption is now searched for the song and any results are offered as candidates in the picker (never confirmed automatically).

Reel Import cleanup: one shared HTTP client and one cookie builder instead of rebuilding them per request, duplicated session/shortcode parsing removed, and unused reel-metadata fields and the never-returned no-match result deleted.

Instagram session handling fixed and hardened: the setting now accepts the whole cookie line (sessionid=…; ds_user_id=…) as well as a bare sessionid, and the app API is called with both sessionid and ds_user_id — the previous build sent a malformed cookie pair, which is why sessions were rejected.
The session test now checks the real logged-in account endpoint instead of a generic one, so a green result means the session actually works for metadata lookups.

Reel Import can now use your own Instagram session: add your sessionid cookie in Settings → Content → Instagram session and metadata lookups run with your logged-in access instead of being blocked (403) — this also makes the official audio API and the reel page work on any network.
When a reel can't be identified without a session, the failure screen now says so and links straight to the setting; the session is validated with a test button and stored only on your device.

Reel Import now reads the song directly from Instagram's official audio API (the same song/artist data the Instagram app shows for licensed audio), with the reel page as fallback — instead of relying on extractor fields that were often missing.
Garbage “matches” are filtered out: machine ids, hashes, JSON fragments and symbol soup returned by the audio fingerprinter or metadata fetches are discarded instead of being offered as songs.
The welcome/support pop-up on first open after an update has been removed.

Reel Import now cleans share links before reading them: tracking parameters like the “?stkn=…” share token are stripped, so metadata and audio-attribution lookups always use the plain reel URL instead of getting JSON error pages.
Importing another reel while the import screen is already open now starts the new search immediately — it no longer reuses the previous reel's search queries.

Reel Import got a visual refresh to match the app theme: a themed gradient background, an animated step-by-step progress view (reel → audio → identify → match), and a song picker that shows up to ten candidates in a themed card with a “N more” hint.

Reel Import no longer guesses the song from creator captions: it uses Instagram's official audio metadata (track/artist, fetched from the reel page when needed) first, then fingerprints the actual audio — captions routinely misname or omit the song.
Fixed a crash when adding a reel's song to a playlist that no longer exists (e.g. a stale default playlist was deleted) — it now falls back to the playlist picker instead of crashing.

Creating a playlist from the reel import flow now reliably adds the song to it — previously the playlist creation could be cancelled before it was saved, leaving the song stranded with a “Couldn't find that song.” error.
Reel Import no longer dead-ends when identification fails: you can jump straight into manual search, and the failure screen tells you what to do next instead of offering a pointless button.
Sharing another reel while the import screen shows a previous result now starts the new import immediately instead of being silently ignored.
Creating a synced playlist while offline no longer crashes — it falls back to a local playlist.
Reel Import now saves every imported song to Recognised Songs (Echo Find history), even when the match came from the caption rather than the fingerprint.
The manual-search box no longer keeps the previous reel's search text when you import another reel.
The playlist picker in Reel Import now offers “Create playlist”, so a fresh install can add the first song without leaving the flow.

Reel Import now listens to the reel's actual audio before trusting the caption: reels whose caption doesn't clearly name a song (hashtags, jokes, foreign text) are fingerprinted instead of being matched against caption guesses, which previously produced wrong or missing results.
Audio fingerprinting now checks two positions in the reel (start and middle) — many reels only play the song after an intro, which the single first-second window missed.
Generic captions like one-word placeholder captions, “Video by …” and credit/disclaimer lines no longer produce false matches.
Reel Import no longer hangs on “Matching on YouTube Music”: every search is now time-boxed, so a slow or flaky connection can't stall the import for minutes before audio fingerprinting even starts.

Song-credit captions (Song Name / Movie / Singers / Composer blocks) are now read properly — the song title is searched without the credit labels, and the best hint is prefilled into manual search when automatic identification finds nothing.
If YouTube Music is unreachable, Reel Import skips the hopeless fingerprint attempt and offers manual search immediately instead of spinning.
Reel Import now actually works end to end: the yt-dlp audio-extraction command was invalid (yt-dlp rejected it instantly), so fingerprinting never ran — fixed and verified against a real reel.
The bundled yt-dlp binary is updated to the latest release on first launch, so Instagram's changing site layout no longer breaks metadata or audio extraction.
Audio excerpts are delivered to the fingerprinter as clean 16-bit PCM (WAV container header stripped), preventing possible recognition failures.
